name: a confusable address that differs only by a +tag: cp.confusable replaces cp.plus_tag
notes: Address claims with a subject: applicable timeProximity 2500, counterpartyExact 3500, counterpartyDomain 1500, subjectOverlap 1500; Σw = 9000. Every pair is exact in time and subject (tp 1, subject 1). The grant binds gmail.sent to acct-a, so NOT_FOUND carries no coverage.account_unbound.

c1 prıya@company.com (dotless ı, U+0131) × o1 prıya+news@company.com: both addresses are confusable (a code point above U+007F, §11), not identical, and differ only by a +tag. §5.1 v1.3: a confusable, non-identical pair scores counterpartyExact 0 with reason cp.confusable, and cp.confusable replaces cp.plus_tag when both apply. counterpartyDomain 0 (it needs neither address to be confusable). S = (2500 + 1500)/9000 = 4000/9000 = 4/9 < 1/2 → not assigned → rule not_found, FINAL, with match.best (4/9) and cp.confusable only.

c2 priya@xn--bcher-kva.example × o2 priya+news@xn--bcher-kva.example: all ASCII, but the xn-- label makes both confusable; again only a +tag differs → cp.confusable, not cp.plus_tag; cd 0 → 4/9 → not_found, FINAL.

c3 raj@company.com × o3 raj+news@company.com (the control: plain ASCII): ce 0 with cp.plus_tag; cd 1 (same non-common domain, only a +tag differs) → S = (2500 + 1500 + 1500)/9000 = 11/18 → partial, FINAL. An implementation that let the +tag rule win for c1 or c2 would give cp.plus_tag and, with cd 1, this 11/18 PARTIAL instead of NOT_FOUND.

c4 lee@XN--bcher-kva.example × o4 lee+news@XN--bcher-kva.example (10:02): §11 v1.3 flags a domain label starting with xn-- in any ASCII case, so both are confusable → cp.confusable, cd 0 → 4/9 → not_found, FINAL. A detector that only knew lowercase 'xn--' would see two plain addresses differing by a +tag on a non-common domain → cp.plus_tag, cd 1 → 11/18 PARTIAL.
All FINAL: the gmail.sent sync at 17:00 ≥ every end + 45. Pairs are two hours apart. o1, o2 and o4 are orphans with no activity → no receipt.
